regions.name: Skull
regions.description: The bony case that protects the brain and supports the face.

regions.name: Spine
regions.description: The column of vertebrae from the neck to the pelvis. It supports the trunk and protects the spinal cord.

considerations.text: The spine lengthens in microgravity and back pain is commonly reported early in flight.

regions.name: Cervical spine
regions.description: The seven vertebrae of the neck.

regions.name: Thoracic spine
regions.description: The twelve vertebrae of the upper and mid back, joined to the ribs.

regions.name: Lumbar spine
regions.description: The five large vertebrae of the lower back.

considerations.text: The spine lengthens in microgravity and back pain is commonly reported early in flight.
Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Rib cage
regions.description: Twelve pairs of ribs that protect the heart and lungs and move with breathing.

regions.name: Pelvis
regions.description: The ring of bones that joins the spine to the legs.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Left clavicle
regions.description: The collarbone, which links the arm to the trunk.

regions.name: Right clavicle
regions.description: The collarbone, which links the arm to the trunk.

regions.name: Left humerus
regions.description: The long bone of the upper arm.

regions.name: Right humerus
regions.description: The long bone of the upper arm.

regions.name: Left femur
regions.description: The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone in the body.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Right femur
regions.description: The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone in the body.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Left knee
regions.description: The hinge joint between the femur and tibia, with the patella in front.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.
Exercise countermeasure hardware has been associated with strain and overuse injuries; record load, device and onset with each pin.

regions.name: Right knee
regions.description: The hinge joint between the femur and tibia, with the patella in front.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.
Exercise countermeasure hardware has been associated with strain and overuse injuries; record load, device and onset with each pin.

regions.name: Left patella
regions.description: The kneecap, a small bone inside the tendon at the front of the knee.

regions.name: Right patella
regions.description: The kneecap, a small bone inside the tendon at the front of the knee.

regions.name: Left tibia
regions.description: The shin bone, which carries most of the body's weight below the knee.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Right tibia
regions.description: The shin bone, which carries most of the body's weight below the knee.

considerations.text: Weight-bearing bones lose mineral density in microgravity unless they are regularly loaded by resistance exercise.

regions.name: Left ankle
regions.description: The joint between the lower leg and the foot.

regions.name: Right ankle
regions.description: The joint between the lower leg and the foot.

regions.name: Left shoulder
regions.description: The deltoid and the muscles around the shoulder joint.

regions.name: Right shoulder
regions.description: The deltoid and the muscles around the shoulder joint.

regions.name: Left forearm
regions.description: The muscles between the elbow and the wrist that move the hand and fingers.

regions.name: Right forearm
regions.description: The muscles between the elbow and the wrist that move the hand and fingers.

regions.name: Left quadriceps
regions.description: The four muscles at the front of the thigh that straighten the knee.

considerations.text: Postural and leg muscles lose mass and strength without load; resistance exercise slows the loss.

regions.name: Right quadriceps
regions.description: The four muscles at the front of the thigh that straighten the knee.

considerations.text: Postural and leg muscles lose mass and strength without load; resistance exercise slows the loss.

regions.name: Left calf
regions.description: The muscles at the back of the lower leg that point the foot.

considerations.text: Postural and leg muscles lose mass and strength without load; resistance exercise slows the loss.

regions.name: Right calf
regions.description: The muscles at the back of the lower leg that point the foot.

considerations.text: Postural and leg muscles lose mass and strength without load; resistance exercise slows the loss.

regions.name: Abdominal wall
regions.description: The layered muscles at the front and sides of the abdomen.

regions.name: Lower back muscles
regions.description: The muscles along the lower spine that hold the trunk upright.

considerations.text: The spine lengthens in microgravity and back pain is commonly reported early in flight.

regions.name: Brain
regions.description: The organ that controls thought, movement, sensation and the body's automatic functions.

regions.name: Spinal cord
regions.description: The bundle of nerves that runs inside the spine and links the brain to the body.

regions.name: Left sciatic nerve
regions.description: The large nerve that runs from the lower back down the back of each leg.

regions.name: Right sciatic nerve
regions.description: The large nerve that runs from the lower back down the back of each leg.

regions.name: Left eye
regions.description: The organ of sight. The optic nerve connects it to the brain.

considerations.text: Fluid shifts toward the head have been linked to changes in eye structure and vision during long-duration flight.

regions.name: Right eye
regions.description: The organ of sight. The optic nerve connects it to the brain.

considerations.text: Fluid shifts toward the head have been linked to changes in eye structure and vision during long-duration flight.

regions.name: Inner ear
regions.description: The organs of hearing and balance inside the skull, on both sides.

considerations.text: The vestibular system adapts to weightlessness; disorientation and motion sickness are most common in the first days and after landing.

regions.name: Heart
regions.description: The muscular pump that moves blood through the lungs and the body.

considerations.text: Headward fluid shift and reduced plasma volume change cardiovascular loading in flight and on return to gravity.

regions.name: Aorta
regions.description: The main artery leaving the heart and running down through the chest and abdomen.

regions.name: Left carotid artery
regions.description: The artery on each side of the neck that supplies the head and brain.

regions.name: Right carotid artery
regions.description: The artery on each side of the neck that supplies the head and brain.

regions.name: Left femoral artery
regions.description: The main artery of the thigh.

regions.name: Right femoral artery
regions.description: The main artery of the thigh.

regions.name: Thorax
regions.description: The chest cavity, holding the lungs, heart and airways.

regions.name: Left lung
regions.description: The organ that brings air into contact with blood to exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

regions.name: Right lung
regions.description: The organ that brings air into contact with blood to exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

regions.name: Trachea
regions.description: The windpipe, which carries air from the throat to the lungs.

regions.name: Diaphragm
regions.description: The dome-shaped muscle under the lungs that drives breathing.

regions.name: Nasal cavity
regions.description: The airway inside the nose. Congestion is common when fluid shifts toward the head.

considerations.text: Headward fluid shift and reduced plasma volume change cardiovascular loading in flight and on return to gravity.

regions.name: Esophagus
regions.description: The muscular tube that carries food from the throat to the stomach.

regions.name: Stomach
regions.description: The organ that stores and starts to digest food.

regions.name: Liver
regions.description: The large organ under the right ribs that processes nutrients and drugs.

regions.name: Small intestine
regions.description: The long, coiled tube where most nutrients are absorbed.

regions.name: Large intestine
regions.description: The final part of the gut, which absorbs water and forms stool.

regions.name: Left kidney
regions.description: The organ that filters blood and makes urine. It sits at the back of the abdomen.

considerations.text: Bone demineralisation raises urinary calcium, which is associated with a higher risk of kidney stones.

regions.name: Right kidney
regions.description: The organ that filters blood and makes urine. It sits at the back of the abdomen.

considerations.text: Bone demineralisation raises urinary calcium, which is associated with a higher risk of kidney stones.

regions.name: Left ureter
regions.description: The tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

regions.name: Right ureter
regions.description: The tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

regions.name: Bladder
regions.description: The organ that stores urine.

regions.name: Spleen
regions.description: The organ under the left ribs that filters blood and supports immune function.

considerations.text: Immune function can change in long-duration flight, including reactivation of latent viruses.

regions.name: Thymus
regions.description: A small organ behind the breastbone that trains immune cells.

regions.name: Cervical lymph nodes
regions.description: Lymph nodes along both sides of the neck.

regions.name: Left axillary lymph nodes
regions.description: Lymph nodes in the armpit.

regions.name: Right axillary lymph nodes
regions.description: Lymph nodes in the armpit.

regions.name: Left inguinal lymph nodes
regions.description: Lymph nodes in the groin.

regions.name: Right inguinal lymph nodes
regions.description: Lymph nodes in the groin.

regions.name: Skin
regions.description: The body's outer covering. It protects, senses and helps control temperature.

considerations.text: Dry air and limited washing in closed habitats are often linked to dry, irritated skin, especially on the hands.

regions.name: Scalp
regions.description: The skin covering the top of the head.

regions.name: Left hand
regions.description: The skin and soft tissue of the hand and fingers.

considerations.text: Dry air and limited washing in closed habitats are often linked to dry, irritated skin, especially on the hands.

regions.name: Right hand
regions.description: The skin and soft tissue of the hand and fingers.

considerations.text: Dry air and limited washing in closed habitats are often linked to dry, irritated skin, especially on the hands.

regions.name: Left foot
regions.description: The skin and soft tissue of the foot. Soles can thin and peel when they carry no weight.

regions.name: Right foot
regions.description: The skin and soft tissue of the foot. Soles can thin and peel when they carry no weight.
